Ms Guru Nanak Earth Movers, --Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. Jai Krishna Pandey, learned
counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Himanshu Sain, learned AGA for
the State.
3. The instant petition is preferred by the
present applicant under Section 528 of BNSS,
2023 against the order of learned C.J.M.,
Bageshwar dated 16.05.2026 passed in Misc.
Application No.17 of 2026 whereby the
application moved by the applicant for
releasing the JS 205 Excavator (JBC) bearing
M/C Serial No.3032182, Engine No.84951880
and Chassis No.PUNJD20AKM3032182 is
rejected.
4. In addition to this the present applicant
is also challenging the revisional order dated
27.07.2026 whereby the revisional court also
dismissed his revision. As it appears from the
order impugned the vehicle in question,
which according to the applicant was seized,
is not the case property of any case.
5. Mr. Himanshu Sain, learned AGA, on
instruction, apprise to this Court that in fact
the vehicle was seized pursuant to an order
passed by the Division Bench in WPPIL
No.202 of 2024 dated 09.01.2025, the relevant
extract of which he has pointed out is

reflected from para 9 of this order, which
reads as under:-
"9. It appears that the Director has issued
orders to his sub-ordinate officers to ensure
compliance of the orders passed by this Court.
Despite the same, mining appears to have
continued on 07th also. Hence, we direct Mr.
Chandra Shekhar Godke, Superintendent of
Police, Bageshwar, who is virtually present
before the Court, to immediately instruct the
Station House Officers under his command
and jurisdiction and also depute the personnel
required to inspect the mines and wherever
machineries are found, the said machineries
shall be seized, and an inventory of all stock
of material shall be drawn up, and shall be
reported to this Court by tomorrow, i.e.
10.01.2025."
6. He have also placed before this Court
the written instruction of the Chowki
Incharge of Kotwali Bageshwar, who has
informed that pursuant to the direction
issued by the Division Bench of this Court in
the WPPIL No.174 of 2024 the vehicle was
seized. Since the vehicle in question is seized
pursuant to an order passed by the Division
Bench of this Court in WPPIL, therefore, the
applicant should move an appropriate
application for releasing such vehicle before
the concerned court dealing with the WPPIL
No.202 of 2024.
7. Thus, I do not find any illegality or
perversity in the order impugned since the
vehicle in question is not the case property
however as per the instructions, as furnished
by learned AGA, the vehicle in question was
seized pursuant to an order passed by the
Division Bench of this Court, therefore the
applicant is at liberty to move a proper

application before the concerned court
dealing with the WPPIL No.202 of 2024.
8. In such view of the matter, the instant
petition is dismissed with a liberty to the
applicant to move a proper application in
WPPIL No.202 of 2024.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
